**Pre-existing on main — fine as a follow-up, not a blocker for this PR.**

A declared `opencode` (export) or `gemini` format gets the wrong checkpoint boundary. Condensation stores a physical line count, but the converter reads `StartLine` as a message index.

- `countTranscriptItems` counts messages only when `agentType` is the built-in `AgentTypeOpenCode` or `AgentTypeGemini`. Every other agent, external forks included, falls through to counting physical lines. The result lands in `CheckpointTranscriptStart`.
- `compactFields` (`checkpoint/persistent.go`) passes that value as `StartLine`. `compactOpenCode` then treats it as a message index and returns nothing once it reaches or passes `len(messages)`.

Repro: the pretty-printed `testdata/opencode_full.jsonl`, with the first checkpoint at 10 messages and the second at all 21:
```
agentType=my-opencode-fork startLine=5724 boundary=21 totalCompactLines=21 slice=0
agentType=OpenCode         startLine=10   boundary=10 totalCompactLines=21 slice=11
```
The external agent's second checkpoint slice is empty.

**Already on main:** the same repro on `main` (95eabf579d) gives identical output. There, format detection sends an external agent's OpenCode export down the same path. This PR doesn't introduce or worsen the bug. It does document `opencode` and `gemini` as declarable values in the external-agent protocol, which points agent authors straight at it.

Suggested follow-up: make `countTranscriptItems` count messages when the agent's declared format (`AsTranscriptFormatProvider`) is `opencode` or `gemini`, or when the format detected for an undeclared transcript is one of those. `opencode-messages`, `codex`, `pi` and the JSONL formats are unaffected, because one line is one item there.

My earlier check missed two findings that the trail reviewers added after it ran. I've fixed one and left the other open for you.

**1. Wrong checkpoint start for OpenCode and Gemini transcripts (low, `manual_commit_condensation.go:1852`): fixed in 36308e9ac2 and resolved.**
- **The bug, which main already has:** an OpenCode export or Gemini session is split into checkpoints by message number. For external agents, though, the CLI counts the transcript by line. From the second checkpoint on, those agents' checkpoint transcripts come out empty.
- **Why it mattered here:** this PR's protocol doc listed `opencode` and `gemini` as formats an agent can declare, which would steer agent authors straight into the bug.
- **Why I didn't fix the count itself:** an agent that keeps its own `compact-transcript` gets the boundary by line (`compact_agent.go:48`), so switching to message counts would break those agents.
- **What I changed instead:** an external agent that declares `opencode` or `gemini` now has the declaration ignored, so it behaves as it does on main today. I added tests for this and updated the protocol doc. The PR description lists fixing the count as a follow-up; after that, the two formats can be accepted.
- I also updated the PR description for the earlier MCP-tool change.

**2. No agent uses `transcript_format` yet (low, `external-agent-protocol.md:81`): left open.** This is a heads-up rather than a bug in this PR. Once a CLI release includes this, the external-agents repo needs three updates:

| Agent | Declares | What it gains |
|---|---|---|
| sarvam | `codex` | per-call model and usage, and exit codes |
| omp | `pi` | the model; tool names change |
| kilo | `opencode-messages` | can drop its own converter |

Each update also has to turn off the agent's own `compact_transcript`. And each agent needs either a minimum CLI version or a working compactor kept for older CLIs, because an older CLI ignores the new field. Resolve that finding, or I can open a tracking issue for it.

content.text:
Because the agent's own compactor always runs first, so a declared format only takes effect when that compactor is off.

The checkpoint write (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:1167-1171`) does this:

```go
compacted, boundary, usedAgent := compactWithAgent(...)   // agent's compact-transcript
if !usedAgent {
    compacted, boundary, err = transcriptcompact.FullWithBoundary(..., compactFields(...))  // built-in, uses transcript_format
}
```

`transcript_format` is only read inside `compactFields`, on the built-in path. If the agent has `compact_transcript` on and its subcommand succeeds, the CLI keeps that output and never reaches the built-in converter. Sarvam would keep writing transcripts without model or usage even though it declares `codex`.

So "has to turn it off" is true of the code as written, not of the protocol itself. The order is a choice I made in this PR, and it causes the version problem from the finding:

- **Compactor off:** an older CLI ignores the format and falls back to detecting it, which fails for omp and kilo.
- **Compactor on:** a newer CLI never uses the declared format.

An agent can't serve both. Flipping the order would fix that: when an agent declares a known format, use the built-in converter, and run the agent's compactor only when it fails or no format is declared. Agents could then keep `compact_transcript` on for older CLIs and also declare a format for newer ones, with no minimum CLI version and nothing to turn off.

The cost is that an agent declaring a format can no longer override the built-in converter with its own. That fits the field's meaning, since declaring it says the CLI's converter fits that transcript.

I'd recommend making that change in this PR, since it's small: a check in `compactWithAgent`, a test, and a doc update. Want me to?
when an agent declares a known format, use the built-in converter - yes we should do this, so is this what you're proposing we do now then?
Yes. I'll make the change now.

content.text:
It's done and pushed in commit 308a61df95: when an agent declares a known format, the CLI now uses its built-in converter first. Lint, the complexity gate, and the transcript, checkpoint and agent tests pass locally. CI and the trail reviewers are running on the new commit now.

**How the CLI picks a converter now** (`compactTranscript` in `checkpoint/persistent.go`):
- **Format declared:** the built-in converter for that format runs first. The agent's own `compact-transcript` runs only if that conversion fails or produces nothing.
- **No format declared:** same as before. The agent's compactor runs first, and the built-in converter is the fallback.

**What this means for agents:** an agent can declare `transcript_format` and keep its own compactor on. A newer CLI uses the built-in converter, and an older CLI, which ignores the field, still uses the agent's compactor. So sarvam, omp and kilo don't have to turn anything off or require a minimum CLI version. They only add the declaration.

**Tests:** I added three checkpoint tests:
- A declared format wins over the agent's own compactor.
- A declared format that converts to nothing falls back to the agent's compactor.
- With no declaration, the agent's compactor still runs first.

With the old order put back, the first of these fails.

I also updated the protocol doc, the PR description and the trail description, which all said to turn the compactor off.

The open adoption finding asks for both of the things this removes: turning the compactor off and a minimum CLI version. Its fix list for the three agents is out of date now. Once the reviewers finish, I can resolve it, pointing to this commit.

No findings are open now. The last one, about external agents not using `transcript_format` yet, is resolved and points to commit 308a61df95. If you'd rather keep it as a reminder, it can be reopened.

What's left:
- **CI on 7f65f0e54d:** still running. The watcher will report the result.
- **Entire Gates:** still waiting on approval from a reviewer.
- **Follow-ups for after this PR:**
  - Once a CLI release includes this, sarvam, omp and kilo each add one `transcript_format` line to their `info` output. They don't need to change anything else.
  - Fix `countTranscriptItems` so that `opencode` and `gemini` can be declared.
why would we need additonal trails for other external agents?

We don't need separate trails. A trail can cover more than one repository (`entire trail link` adds another repository's branch), so the agent updates can be a second change on trail 2957.

They also don't have to wait for a release anymore. That was true only while agents had to turn their own compactor off. Now each agent just adds `transcript_format` to its `info` output and keeps its compactor:
- **CLI versions before this one** ignore the field and keep using the agent's compactor, so nothing changes there.
- **This CLI and newer** use the built-in converter.

That makes the external-agents branch safe to merge at any time. It only takes effect once a CLI with this change is released.

One thing to decide per agent: for omp, the built-in output keeps native tool names (`Write`, `mcp:read`), while omp's own compactor lowercases them and strips `mcp:`. For sarvam and kilo the built-in output is the same or better.

I'd add the three declarations on a branch in external-agents and link it to this trail:

| Agent | Declares |
|---|---|
| sarvam | `codex` |
| omp | `pi` |
| kilo | `opencode-messages` |

Want me to do that?
why do we need that? shouldn't this auotmatically take care of that?

It can't be fully automatic, for two reasons.

**1. Without a declaration, the agent's own compactor runs first.** All three agents ship a `compact-transcript`, and when they don't declare a format the CLI uses that compactor and never tries its own converter. That order is deliberate: an agent author who wrote a compactor presumably did so because the CLI's converter didn't fit. The CLI shouldn't override that by guessing from the content.

**2. Guessing from the content fails for two of the three agents:**
- **omp:** writes a title line before the Pi header, so the CLI doesn't recognize it as Pi. It falls through to Claude/Cursor-style JSONL and loses the model.
- **kilo:** stores one OpenCode message per line. The CLI never auto-detects that layout, so it converts to nothing.
- **sarvam:** is the only one detection would get right, since it's a Codex rollout.

So "prefer the built-in converter when detection works" would help sarvam only. It would also put the other two at risk, because detection never reports failure: anything unrecognized falls back to Claude/Cursor-style JSONL. The CLI can't tell a confident match from that fallback, so it would sometimes replace a working agent compactor with a wrong conversion.

Declaring the format is how an agent says "my transcript is exactly this format", which is the one thing the CLI can't reliably work out itself. It's a one-line change per agent, and it can't break anything.
can we do that in this trail?
Yes. I'll create a branch in the external-agents repo and link it to trail 2957.
